tools.name: PDF Compressor
tools.description: Compress a PDF and compare the actual savings.
tools.intro: Make a PDF lighter on your device with Recommended, Strong compression or Best quality. Compare actual original and compressed sizes; download is offered only when the result is meaningfully smaller.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB.
Keep Recommended or choose Strong compression / Best quality, then select Compress PDF.
Compare Original, Compressed and Saved values, review the PDF and download the smaller file.
tools.help: Automatic compression first optimizes PDF structure without rasterizing text. Plain scanned documents can be recompressed using the selected quality level; text, forms, links, outlines and vector content are protected from automatic page-image conversion. If a tested copy is not smaller, the tool may try a more compact scan configuration and keeps the best result. Changes below 1% or 256 bytes are treated as negligible. An equal or larger copy is never offered as compressed output. Advanced settings retain structural-only optimization and an explicit image-copy option with resolution and JPEG quality controls. Image-copy mode removes selectable text, links, forms and accessibility tags. Scan rendering is limited to 40 pages, 6 million pixels per page and 60 million pixels total; structural optimization supports 500 pages. Password-protected PDFs are unsupported, and digital-signature validity is not preserved. Originals stay unchanged.

faq.question: Which compression level should I choose?
faq.answer: Recommended balances size and quality. Strong compression targets smaller scanned files; Best quality uses a lighter reduction. Normal use does not require resolution or JPEG settings.

faq.question: Will every PDF become smaller?
faq.answer: No. Already optimized PDFs may have no meaningful reduction. Larger or nearly identical copies are discarded; the tool tells you to keep the original.

faq.question: Does compression remove searchable text?
faq.answer: Automatic mode retains text and document features. The explicit image-copy option under Advanced settings replaces all pages with pictures and removes text search and selection.

seo.title: Compress PDF Online — Reduce File Size
seo.description: Reduce PDF file size with simple compression levels. Compare original size and savings, and download only a meaningfully smaller result. Files stay on-device.

next.reason: Need only a few pages? Extract them before compressing.
Combine related files before making the final document smaller.

tools.name: PDF Merger
tools.description: Bring multiple PDFs into one document.
tools.intro: Combine two or more PDFs into one document locally. Check page counts, reorder the files and download a merged PDF without a paid API or server upload.
steps: Choose two to ten unencrypted PDFs, up to 20 MB each and 40 MB total.
Use the up/down controls to set document order.
Merge the PDFs, check the output page count and download the new document.
tools.help: Pages are copied in document order with pdf-lib running in a background worker. The output is limited to 500 pages. Original files remain unchanged. Interactive forms, bookmarks and digital signatures may not carry over to the new PDF. Password-protected documents are rejected. Review the downloaded pages before using the result. This operation combines files; it does not promise smaller file sizes.

faq.question: Are my PDFs uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The merger processes them in a worker on your device. The processing library is downloaded only for PDF tools.

faq.question: Can I change file order?
faq.answer: Yes. After choosing files, use the up/down controls beside each document. Pages inside each source document remain in their original order.

faq.question: Will forms and digital signatures remain valid?
faq.answer: This tool copies page content and does not guarantee interactive forms or bookmarks. Creating a new PDF does not preserve digital-signature validity. Review the output.

seo.title: Merge PDF Files — Combine Documents in Order
seo.description: Combine multiple PDFs into one document. Check page counts, choose file order and download a merged PDF with local browser processing.

tools.name: PDF Splitter
tools.description: Extract the pages you actually need.
tools.intro: Extract selected PDF pages into one new document. Choose individual pages or ranges, control their order and download the result, with processing on your device.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB.
Enter pages or ranges, such as 1, 3-5, 8.
Extract the selection and download the resulting PDF.
tools.help: Page numbers start at 1. Ranges must run in ascending order, but separate selections can be arranged in your preferred order, such as 5, 1-3. Duplicate or out-of-range pages are rejected. The selected pages become one PDF; this version does not create a ZIP of separate documents. Input and output are limited to 500 pages. Interactive forms, bookmarks and digital signatures may not carry over. Password-protected PDFs are unsupported.

faq.question: Does this make one PDF or many?
faq.answer: It makes one PDF containing the selected pages in the order entered. Repeat the operation for another selection if you need separate documents.

faq.question: Can I reorder pages while extracting?
faq.answer: Yes. For example, 5, 1-3 places page 5 first, followed by pages 1, 2 and 3.

faq.question: Can I extract pages from a protected PDF?
faq.answer: No. Use an unencrypted document you are authorized to process. This tool does not remove passwords.

seo.title: Split PDF — Extract Selected Pages
seo.description: Extract individual pages or page ranges into a new PDF. Set the selection order and keep your original document unchanged. Processing stays in your browser.

tools.name: PDF to PNG/JPG
tools.description: Export PDF pages as JPG or PNG images.
tools.intro: Export selected PDF pages as JPG or PNG files locally. Choose resolution, preview actual page images, and download them individually or together in a ZIP.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB.
Select pages or ranges, image format and resolution.
Convert, review the previews and download the images or ZIP.
tools.help: Leave the page selection empty to export all pages, or enter a selection such as 1, 3-5. Pages are rendered with PDF.js at 96, 144 or 192 DPI. JPG uses adjustable lossy quality; PNG is lossless and can be larger. Output has a white background. Rendering is limited to 40 pages, 6 million pixels per page, 60 million pixels total and 40 MB of images. Image files do not retain interactive PDF links, forms or selectable text.

faq.question: Can I export PNG instead of JPG?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose PNG in the image-format selector. Each page is also available as an individual download.

faq.question: Why is a high-resolution conversion rejected?
faq.answer: Rendering uses device memory. Choose a lower resolution or fewer pages to stay within the stated pixel and output limits.

seo.title: PDF to JPG or PNG — Export Page Images
seo.description: Turn PDF pages into PNG or JPG images on your device. Choose the pages and resolution, then download the rendered images without a file upload.

next.reason: Change exported image dimensions for a specific pixel limit.
Compare a smaller image copy before sharing it.

tools.name: PNG/JPG to PDF
tools.description: Combine JPG and PNG images into a PDF.
tools.intro: Combine JPG and PNG images into one PDF without uploading them. Set their order, page size, orientation, fitting and margins, then download a document with one image per page.
steps: Choose up to 20 JPG or PNG images, at most 20 MB each and 40 MB total.
Drag the images or use the arrow controls to set order, then choose page size, orientation, fitting and margins.
Create the PDF, check its page count and download.
tools.help: Auto Image Size uses 0.75 PDF points per pixel plus margins. Choose Auto, Portrait or Landscape orientation for image-size, A4 or Letter pages. Fit keeps the whole image inside the margins; Fill crops the edges to cover that area. Both preserve aspect ratio. JPEG data is embedded; PNG supports transparency. There is no OCR or selectable text. Each input is limited to 20 million pixels and the combined selection to 60 million pixels. Original images remain unchanged.

faq.question: Can I mix JPG and PNG files?
faq.answer: Yes. Both formats can be combined in one document, with one image on each page.

faq.question: Will the image be cropped?
faq.answer: Fit preserves the whole image and may leave white space. Fill preserves proportions but crops edges to cover the page area.

seo.title: JPG & PNG to PDF — Combine Your Images
seo.description: Combine JPG and PNG images into a PDF in your chosen order. Set page layout, inspect the result and download the document without uploading your files.

next.reason: Trim unwanted borders before combining your images.
Combine the resulting PDF with another document.

tools.name: PDF to Word
tools.description: Convert PDF text into editable Word with preserved page layout.
tools.intro: Convert selectable PDF text into editable Word paragraphs, headings and recoverable tables while preserving source page sizes, page boundaries and positions. Complex diagrams remain localized images.
steps: Choose an unencrypted text-based PDF up to 20 MB and 40 pages. Scanned PDFs belong in the separate PDF OCR tool.
Select Convert to Word. Native text, layout and drawing information are analyzed locally; real page progress appears below the button.
Download the editable DOCX and review page layout, tables and any font substitutions in your Word editor.
tools.help: Editable Word conversion is the only mode. Native PDF text is grouped into lines and paragraphs using physical coordinates, font sizes and styles. Editable Word text containers retain line breaks, indentation and intentional blank space; source pages receive explicit section boundaries with matching dimensions. Recoverable ruled tables become real Word tables with editable cell text. Embedded images and complex vector regions such as architecture diagrams and charts are preserved as localized high-resolution images, with surrounding text remaining editable. Complete pages are never inserted as screenshots. Headers, footers and saved page numbers retain their source positions as editable text rather than recalculated fields. This is not the Microsoft Word layout engine: font substitution, uncommon writing directions, borderless/merged tables, complex overlapping artwork and major edits to fixed text containers can change appearance. Rotated text and oversized or overly complex pages are rejected with a useful message. Scanned/image-only pages are directed to the separate OCR workflow; OCR is never loaded or invoked here. Limits are 20 MB input, 40 pages, 200,000 native text characters, 22 inches per page side and 40 MB output. Files stay on your device; the PDF engine loads only when needed.

faq.question: Can I edit the text in the Word document?
faq.answer: Yes. Selectable PDF text becomes genuine Word paragraphs in positioned text containers. Recoverable ruled tables have editable cells. Images and complex diagrams remain images.

faq.question: Are architecture diagrams and charts preserved?
faq.answer: Complex vector drawing regions are rendered locally at high resolution and placed in their original area. The entire page is not rasterized, and the surrounding text remains editable.

faq.question: Will text move from one source page into another?
faq.answer: Each source page receives an explicit Word section boundary and matching physical dimensions. Original positions and blank space are retained. Large edits or differences between Word editors can still affect fixed text containers.

faq.question: Does this use OCR for a normal PDF?
faq.answer: No. Only native PDF text and drawing information are used. Scanned/image-only PDFs show a message directing you to the separate PDF OCR tool.

faq.question: Will the result match every PDF perfectly?
faq.answer: No. PDF and Word use different layout models. Review font substitutions, complex tables and unusual graphics before sharing the result.

faq.question: Are documents uploaded?
faq.answer: No. PDF analysis, localized graphic rendering and DOCX packaging run locally on your device.

seo.title: PDF to Word — Editable DOCX from Native PDF Text
seo.description: Convert selectable PDF text into editable Word text, retaining page boundaries, recoverable tables and diagrams. No OCR. Complex layouts may need adjustment.

next.reason: Scanned pages have no native text to convert. Use recognition for editable text.
After editing your DOCX, create a PDF copy to share.

tools.name: PDF OCR
tools.description: Extract structured English text from scanned PDF pages.
tools.intro: Extract structured English text from a scanned PDF on your device. Recognize pages one at a time, review paragraphs and readable table rows, then copy text or download TXT and editable DOCX.
steps: Choose an unencrypted scanned PDF. Mobile supports 5 pages / 5 MB; desktop supports 10 pages / 10 MB.
Select Extract text to load the local English OCR engine. Real page and recognition progress appear below the button.
Review names, numbers and reading order, then copy or download structured text or Word output.
tools.help: PDF OCR is separate from native PDF to Word. Pages are rendered sequentially with bounded image sizes. Preparation can upscale small text, correct clearly sideways text, normalize low contrast and let the engine correct small skew. Clear pages avoid destructive thresholding. Recognized word and line boxes are grouped into paragraphs, heading size hierarchy, lists, readable aligned rows and column-first reading order. Only recognized content is included. Complex forms, irregular tables, handwriting, non-English scripts, ambiguous orientation and poor scans remain limited; check every important number. Each recognized page remains a corresponding DOCX section. Only engine and English language assets are downloaded; your files are never uploaded. Cancel terminates the worker, and temporary page canvases are released after each page.

faq.question: When should I use PDF OCR?
faq.answer: Use it for image-only scans without selectable text. For a normal PDF with real text, use PDF to Word to preserve its native text and font information.

faq.question: Can I download an editable Word document?
faq.answer: Yes. Reconstructed paragraphs, lists and simple aligned tables are packaged into a DOCX. Review recognition mistakes and complex layouts.

faq.question: Which languages and limits are supported?
faq.answer: English printed text. Mobile supports 5 pages / 5 MB; desktop supports 10 pages / 10 MB. Split larger documents first.

faq.question: Does the OCR engine load during normal conversion?
faq.answer: No. It initializes only after you explicitly select Extract text in an OCR tool. Native PDF to Word and Word to PDF never invoke OCR.

seo.title: PDF OCR — Extract Text from Scanned Pages
seo.description: Recognize English printed text in scanned PDF pages locally. Review structured paragraphs, then copy or export TXT and editable DOCX.

next.reason: Already selectable text? Convert the native text without OCR.
Recognize a single JPG or PNG scan instead.

tools.name: Word to PDF
tools.description: Create a PDF from a DOCX with selectable text.
tools.intro: Convert a DOCX into a PDF with selectable text using its actual paragraphs, runs, styles, tables and images. Preserve explicit page breaks, saved page boundaries and section margins without OCR.
steps: Choose a DOCX up to 20 MB. Save older DOC files as DOCX first.
Wait for local preparation and review the supported structure and limitations.
Convert to PDF, then check page breaks, spacing and font substitutions before downloading.
tools.help: DOCX is parsed directly as Office Open XML. Page breaks within runs, page-break-before paragraph styles, saved last-rendered-page-break markers and next/odd/even section boundaries are respected. Section-specific sizes and margins, intentional empty paragraphs, exact/minimum line spacing, paragraph spacing and indentation are retained. Basic keep-next/keep-lines, alignments, bold/italic/underlined runs, colors, lists, tables, PNG/JPEG images, saved header/footer text and page/margin-anchored image offsets are supported. Content is not packed into earlier pages across saved boundaries. Liberation Sans fonts are embedded; this is not the Microsoft Word layout engine, so pagination without saved boundaries, custom fonts, multi-column sections, complex header/footer drawings, merged/nested tables, tracked edits and unusual floating objects can differ. Dynamic fields use saved text rather than recalculation. No OCR or page screenshot conversion is involved. Limits: 20 MB input, 32 MB expanded archive, 200,000 body text characters, 100 output pages and 40 MB PDF output. No file upload or conversion service is used.

faq.question: Does Word to PDF ever use OCR?
faq.answer: No. DOCX already contains structured text and images. It is parsed and rendered natively, without recognition.

faq.question: Will page 2 move into blank space on page 1?
faq.answer: Explicit page/section breaks and saved page-boundary markers prevent that. Intentional empty paragraphs and spacing are preserved. Documents lacking saved pagination can still wrap differently because browser-side font metrics differ from Microsoft Word.

faq.question: Are headers and footers supported?
faq.answer: Simple saved paragraph text, alignment and first-page variants are supported. Dynamic fields are not recalculated, and complex drawings/tables in headers or footers need review.

faq.question: Are older DOC files supported?
faq.answer: No. Save them as DOCX in a compatible editor first.

seo.title: Word to PDF — Convert DOCX with Page Breaks
seo.description: Convert DOCX to PDF on your device. Preserve explicit page breaks, margins, text, tables and images where supported. No OCR or document upload.

next.reason: Check whether the exported PDF can be made smaller.
Combine the finished document with another PDF.

tools.name: Rotate PDF
tools.description: Turn selected pages the right way up.
tools.intro: Rotate selected PDF pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees clockwise. Keep the original document and download a separate rotated copy.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB and 500 pages.
Enter the pages to rotate and choose a clockwise angle.
Rotate and review the downloaded copy.
tools.help: Page numbers start at 1. Enter individual pages and ranges, such as 1, 3-5. Rotation is added to each page’s existing orientation; page content is not turned into images. Editing a PDF invalidates its digital signatures. Review page orientation after downloading.

faq.question: Can I rotate only one page?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter that page’s number instead of a range.

faq.question: Does rotation change image quality?
faq.answer: No rasterization is performed. This operation adjusts PDF page rotation.

seo.title: Rotate PDF Pages — Choose Pages and Angle
seo.description: Rotate selected PDF pages by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. Create a separate copy without rasterizing page content or uploading your document.

tools.name: Delete PDF Pages
tools.description: Remove unwanted pages from a document.
tools.intro: Remove unwanted pages from a PDF and download the remaining pages in their original order. Processing happens in a worker on your device.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB and 500 pages.
Enter the page numbers or ranges to remove.
Create the remaining document, check its page count and download.
tools.help: For example, 2, 5-7 removes pages 2, 5, 6 and 7. At least one page must remain. Duplicate and out-of-range page numbers are rejected. Pages are copied into a new PDF; interactive forms, bookmarks and digital signatures may not carry over. Check the result before sharing.

faq.question: Are my original pages deleted permanently?
faq.answer: No. Your source file is unchanged. The tool creates a separate PDF containing the remaining pages.

seo.title: Delete PDF Pages — Keep Only What You Need
seo.description: Remove selected PDF pages or ranges and save the remaining document. Your original stays unchanged, with processing in a browser worker.

tools.name: Reorder PDF Pages
tools.description: Arrange every page in your preferred order.
tools.intro: Arrange every page of a PDF in the order you need. Enter an explicit page sequence and create a separate reordered document locally.
steps: Choose an unencrypted PDF up to 20 MB and 500 pages.
Enter every page exactly once in the required order, for example 3, 1-2.
Create the document, review its order and download.
tools.help: Ranges run in ascending order within each range, but separate selections can be rearranged. A three-page document can use 3, 1-2 to put page 3 first. Missing, duplicate and out-of-range pages are rejected. To keep only some pages, use PDF Splitter instead. Page copying may omit forms and bookmarks, and digital signatures are not preserved.

faq.question: Can I leave out a page?
faq.answer: Reorder requires all pages exactly once. Use PDF Splitter to extract a subset or Delete PDF Pages to remove pages.

seo.title: Reorder PDF Pages — Set an Exact Page Sequence
seo.description: Arrange every page of a PDF in your chosen order. Enter individual pages or ranges and download a separate document processed locally.

tools.name: Image Compressor
tools.description: Compress, compare and download a lighter image.
tools.intro: Adjust output format, quality and optional maximum width, then compare the original and compressed image. File size, bytes saved and percentage change are calculated from the actual output.
steps: Choose an image and review its original size and dimensions.
Choose an output format, adjust quality where available, and optionally limit width.
Compress, compare the two previews and actual sizes, then download the result.
tools.help: JPEG, WebP and supported AVIF encoders use adjustable lossy quality. PNG is lossless; reducing dimensions or changing format may be needed to reduce size. BMP is uncompressed and is generally unsuitable for smaller downloads. The compressor never upscales an image. Some optimized originals become larger after processing; the result shows this clearly. Maximum output is 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side. Metadata and animation are not preserved.

faq.question: Does every image become smaller?
faq.answer: No. Already optimized files may become larger. The savings panel uses the original and output byte counts, and flags a larger result.

faq.question: Why is there no PNG quality slider?
faq.answer: The browser PNG encoder does not use the lossy quality setting. Reduce dimensions or try JPEG/WebP when suitable.

faq.question: Where is compression performed?
faq.answer: On your device, using a background worker and OffscreenCanvas where supported. A smaller compatibility fallback supports older browsers. Files are not uploaded.

seo.title: Image Compressor — Compare Real File Size Savings
seo.description: Compress an image with format, quality and maximum-width controls. Compare actual sizes and previews before downloading. Image contents stay on your device.

next.reason: Use dimensions when the requirement is a pixel limit, rather than a byte limit.
Combine JPG or PNG images into a document.

tools.name: Image Resizer
tools.description: Set dimensions, choose a format and resize precisely.
tools.intro: Resize an image with width and height controls, an aspect-ratio lock and useful presets. Choose Fit, Fill or Stretch, then export a supported format without uploading your file.
steps: Choose an image and check its original dimensions, format and size.
Set a preset or width and height. Use the aspect lock or choose Fit, Fill or Stretch.
Select the output format and quality, resize, review the preview and download.
tools.help: Fit preserves proportions inside a bounding box. Fill crops from the center to match both dimensions. Stretch changes proportions. Presets set a bounding box; Fit may produce smaller dimensions to preserve the original ratio. Output is limited to 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side; input is limited to 20 MB and 40 million pixels. A compatibility fallback is limited to 4 million pixels. JPEG and BMP fill transparent areas with white. Metadata and animation are not retained. Enlarging cannot restore missing detail.

faq.question: How does aspect-ratio locking work?
faq.answer: When locked, changing width recalculates height and changing height recalculates width. Unlock it to enter an independent bounding box, or use Fill and Stretch for exact output dimensions.

faq.question: Why does Fit differ from a preset size?
faq.answer: A preset defines a bounding box. Fit keeps the original proportions inside it. Choose Fill for exact dimensions with center cropping, or Stretch if distortion is acceptable.

faq.question: Can I keep transparency?
faq.answer: Yes, select PNG or a supported WebP/AVIF output. JPEG and BMP use a white background.

seo.title: Image Resizer — Set Width, Height and Aspect Ratio
seo.description: Resize images in pixels with an aspect-ratio lock, presets and Fit, Fill or Stretch options. Preview and download a locally processed image.

next.reason: Reduce file size after setting the required dimensions.
Select a specific region rather than resizing the entire image.

tools.name: Image Converter
tools.description: Convert between supported image formats locally.
tools.intro: Convert a supported image to JPEG, PNG, WebP, BMP or browser-supported AVIF. One shared on-device engine handles your format selection and creates an actual downloadable file.
steps: Choose an image and check the original format and dimensions.
Select a supported output format and adjust quality where meaningful.
Convert, compare the original and result, and download the new file.
tools.help: Supported inputs are JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP and GIF when the browser can decode them. GIF uses its first frame; animated export is not supported. AVIF output is shown only after an actual encoder check. PNG/WebP/AVIF can retain transparency; JPEG and 24-bit BMP use white. BMP output is uncompressed and often much larger. The converter preserves dimensions but strips metadata. Files must be at most 20 MB; output is capped at 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side. Use the Image Resizer first for a larger image. HEIC/HEIF and TIFF/TIF require additional decoders and are not accepted in this version.

faq.question: Can I convert JPG to PNG or PNG to WebP?
faq.answer: Yes. Upload the supported source image and choose PNG or a browser-supported WebP output. JPEG and JPG refer to the same format.

faq.question: Can I convert HEIC, TIFF or animated GIFs?
faq.answer: HEIC and TIFF are not supported. GIF input is decoded as a still first frame, and its animation is not preserved.

faq.question: Why is AVIF not listed in my browser?
faq.answer: Decoding AVIF and encoding it are different capabilities. The tool offers AVIF output only if a small real encoding test returns an AVIF file.

seo.title: Image Converter — JPG, PNG, WebP, BMP & AVIF
seo.description: Convert supported images to JPG, PNG, WebP or BMP, with AVIF export when your browser supports it. Compare the real output before downloading.

next.reason: Use PNG for a lossless copy; it cannot restore detail lost in a JPG.
Use JPEG for photographs when transparency is not needed.

tools.name: Image Cropper
tools.description: Select precise pixels and export a cropped image.
tools.intro: Choose the exact portion of an image to keep using a draggable selection, resize handles or precise pixel coordinates. Export the crop in a supported image format on your device.
steps: Choose an image and review its original dimensions.
Drag or resize the crop selection, choose a preset, or enter precise original-image pixel coordinates.
Check the highlighted selection, choose the format, crop and download.
tools.help: Drag the selection to move it, or drag a corner to resize it. Focus the handles and use arrow keys for one-pixel steps or Shift for ten. Left and top start at zero. The selected rectangle must stay inside the source image and use whole-number pixels. Presets create a centered square, 16:9 or 4:3 selection. Cropping keeps the selected pixels without padding or resizing. Input is limited to 20 MB and 40 million pixels; output to 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side. JPEG/BMP fill transparency with white. Metadata and animation are not retained.

faq.question: Does cropping resize the image?
faq.answer: No. Output dimensions match your crop width and height. Use Image Resizer for a different final size.

faq.question: Can I keep a transparent background?
faq.answer: Choose PNG or a supported WebP/AVIF output. JPEG and BMP do not support transparency.

seo.title: Image Cropper — Drag or Enter Exact Pixel Bounds
seo.description: Crop an image using a draggable selection, presets or precise pixel coordinates. Keep the selected area and export a supported format locally.

tools.name: JPG to PNG
tools.description: Convert photographs to PNG format.
tools.intro: Convert a JPG photograph into a PNG on your device. This focused converter starts with PNG selected and keeps the original dimensions, with a real preview and download.
steps: Choose a JPG or another supported image up to 20 MB.
Keep PNG selected; review the original dimensions and preview.
Convert the image, compare the actual file size and download the PNG.
tools.help: PNG uses lossless encoding, but converting an already compressed JPEG does not recover detail lost earlier. Photographs often become larger as PNG. The source background stays opaque; this conversion cannot remove a background or create transparency. The shared image engine keeps dimensions and exports real PNG bytes. Metadata and animation are not retained. Output is limited to 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side.

faq.question: Will a PNG improve the quality of my JPG?
faq.answer: No. PNG avoids further lossy encoding, but cannot restore detail already discarded by JPEG.

faq.question: Does JPG to PNG make the background transparent?
faq.answer: No. The original background remains part of the image. This tool changes the file format.

seo.title: JPG to PNG — Convert Without Changing Dimensions
seo.description: Create a PNG copy of a JPG image in your browser. Keep the dimensions and inspect the result. Conversion cannot restore detail already lost in JPEG.

tools.name: PNG to JPG
tools.description: Make a JPEG from your PNG image.
tools.intro: Create a JPEG copy of a PNG image locally. Adjust JPEG quality, keep the image dimensions and compare the real output before downloading.
steps: Choose a PNG or another supported image up to 20 MB.
Keep JPEG selected and choose the quality you need.
Convert, review the preview and byte count, then download the JPG.
tools.help: JPEG is often smaller for photographs and uses lossy compression. It is less suitable for crisp diagrams and text. PNG transparency is filled with white because JPEG cannot store alpha transparency. A higher quality setting usually gives a larger file; no specific saving is promised. Original files are unchanged. Metadata and animation are not preserved. Input is limited to 40 million pixels; output to 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side.

faq.question: What happens to transparent PNG areas?
faq.answer: They are composited onto a white background in the JPEG output.

faq.question: Will every PNG become smaller?
faq.answer: No. Size depends on the image and quality setting. Compare the actual byte counts before choosing the result.

seo.title: PNG to JPG — Choose JPEG Quality
seo.description: Convert PNG to JPG with adjustable quality and a real file-size comparison. Transparent areas become white. Your source image remains unchanged.

tools.name: WebP Converter
tools.description: Switch images to a modern web format.
tools.intro: Convert an image to WebP with a quality setting and real size comparison. WebP is selected initially, with processing and previews kept on your device.
steps: Choose a supported image up to 20 MB.
Keep WebP selected and set its quality.
Convert, inspect the preview and download the WebP copy.
tools.help: WebP supports transparency and lossy encoding for photographs. Smaller output depends on the source and quality; the tool reports actual bytes. Browser support is checked by creating a real encoded file. If your browser cannot export WebP, use another offered format in Image Converter. Input GIF uses the first frame, and animation and metadata are not retained. Output is limited to 16 million pixels and 8,000 pixels per side.

faq.question: Can WebP keep transparency?
faq.answer: Yes. Supported WebP export preserves image transparency.

faq.question: Can this convert an animated GIF into animated WebP?
faq.answer: No. This version exports a single image frame; it does not preserve animation.

seo.title: WebP Converter — Create a WebP Image
seo.description: Convert supported images to WebP, adjust quality and compare actual sizes. Transparency is supported; animated input produces a single still frame.

tools.name: Image to Text OCR
tools.description: Extract readable text from an image.
tools.intro: Extract English printed text from a PNG or JPEG image using OCR on your device. Review the recognized words, copy them or download structured TXT and editable DOCX.
steps: Choose a clear, upright PNG or JPEG containing English text.
Select Extract text; the local OCR engine loads on demand and shows real recognition progress.
Check spelling, numbers and reading order, then copy or download TXT or Word output.
tools.help: OCR recognizes shapes rather than reading an original text layer. Photos, small fonts, tilted pages and handwriting can cause mistakes. English is the supported recognition language in this version. Mobile input limits are 5 MB and 12 million pixels; desktop limits are 10 MB and 20 million pixels. Prepared images are capped at 1.8 million OCR pixels on mobile or 3 million on desktop. Small text can be upscaled, clearly sideways text corrected and low contrast normalized. Already-clear pages avoid hard binarization. Word/line boxes reconstruct paragraph groups, column-first reading order and simple aligned tables; complex layouts still need review. The pinned Tesseract engine and English language asset load only when you start recognition. Cancel or reset terminates the worker. No file is uploaded, no account is needed, and unreadable images do not produce an empty successful result.

faq.question: Which OCR languages are supported?
faq.answer: English printed text is supported. Other scripts and mixed-language pages may be recognized incorrectly.

faq.question: Are images sent to an OCR service?
faq.answer: No. Image preparation and recognition run locally. The browser downloads the OCR engine and English language data only when requested.

faq.question: Can OCR read handwriting or guarantee correct numbers?
faq.answer: No. Clear printed text works best. Review names, numbers and punctuation carefully.

tools.name: GPA Calculator

Add a row for every course in the semester.
Read your weighted GPA and total credits.
tools.help: GPA = sum of (course credits × grade points) ÷ total credits. A three-credit course carries more weight than a one-credit course. This calculator accepts points from 0 to 10; use your institution’s actual scale.

faq.question: Does it support a 4.0 scale?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter your actual grade points between 0 and 4. The calculator also accepts other scales up to 10.

faq.question: Are all courses weighted equally?

steps: Enter each semester’s GPA and completed credits.
Add all semesters you want to include.
Review your CGPA and the total credits.
tools.help: CGPA = sum of (semester GPA × semester credits) ÷ total credits. Averaging semester GPAs without weighting is only correct when every semester has the same number of credits. Your institution may treat repeats differently.

faq.question: Can I just average my semester GPAs?
faq.answer: Only if every semester has equal credits. This calculator weights each semester by its credit total.

tools.help: Current percentage is obtained marks divided by completed total, multiplied by 100. Target marks use the completed and remaining totals together. faq.question: Can I find what I need in a final exam?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter marks obtained so far, the completed total and the marks available in the final. Set your target overall percentage.

tools.name: Attendance Calculator

steps: Enter whole numbers of classes attended and held.
Choose the attendance percentage you need.
Review the current percentage and future-class estimate.
tools.help: Attendance equals attended divided by held, multiplied by 100. Future-class estimates add each new class to both counts and round the required number upward. Allowed absences add classes only to the held count and round downward. Once you have missed a class, exactly 100% attendance cannot be restored by a finite number of additional classes. The estimate excludes cancelled classes, excused absences and institution-specific policies.

faq.question: Does it assume I attend all future classes?
faq.answer: Yes. The catch-up estimate assumes every additional class is attended.

faq.question: Why can I not recover 100% attendance?
faq.answer: A previously missed class remains in the total. Your percentage can approach 100% but cannot equal it with a finite number of new classes.

tools.help: Choose a country for sensible currency and unit defaults; currency can be overridden. Country changes clear numeric inputs to avoid reinterpreting them in new units. Fuel needed is multiplied by the price per litre, US gallon or Imperial gallon. One US gallon is 3.785411784 litres and one Imperial gallon is 4.54609 litres; one mile is 1.609344 kilometres. Include both directions for a return trip. Traffic, weather and driving conditions can change actual consumption. Tolls and parking are not included.

faq.question: Does it fetch current fuel prices?
faq.answer: No. Enter the price you want to use. The calculator does not assume a current market rate.

faq.question: Which gallon is used for MPG?
faq.answer: Separate US and Imperial options are labeled explicitly. A US gallon is 3.785411784 litres; an Imperial gallon is 4.54609 litres. Select the convention your vehicle figures use.

faq.question: Can I split the journey cost?

seo.title: Fuel Cost Calculator — Trip Cost in Your Units

tools.name: University Merit Calculator

steps: Enter the obtained and total marks for each component.

tools.help: Each component contributes obtained marks divided by total marks, multiplied by its weight. The contributions add into a final percentage. Up to ten components are supported. The example School, College and Admission Test rows are illustrative, not the rules of a specific university. This tool does not apply eligibility requirements, quotas, bonus marks, conversion policies or changing admission thresholds.

faq.question: Are the default weights official?
faq.answer: No. They are examples. Enter the current formula from the university you are applying to.

faq.question: Does the result guarantee admission?
faq.answer: No. It calculates an aggregate only. Eligibility and selection depend on the institution’s rules.

tools.name: Age Calculator

tools.intro: Calculate calendar age in years, months and days between a birth date and an as-of date. Also see the number of elapsed days.
steps: Enter the birth date.
Choose the date to calculate age on; today is selected initially.
Read the calendar age and elapsed-day total.
tools.help: The calculation uses Gregorian calendar dates without time-of-day or time-zone offsets. An anniversary on a missing day is clamped to the last day of that month; February 29 uses February 28 in a non-leap year. Elapsed days do not include the start date. Future birth dates relative to the as-of date are rejected. This is a date calculation, not a legal determination of age.

faq.question: Can I calculate age on a past date?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the as-of date to any valid date on or after the birth date.

faq.question: How are leap-day birthdays handled?
faq.answer: In a non-leap year, the calendar anniversary is treated as February 28. Legal rules may differ.

seo.title: Age Calculator — Years, Months and Days
seo.description: Calculate age between a birth date and an as-of date. See years, months, days and elapsed days using calendar dates without time-zone offsets.

tools.name: Loan / EMI Calculator
tools.description: Estimate regular loan repayments.
tools.intro: Estimate a fixed monthly loan payment from an amount, annual interest rate and term. See the total repayment and interest using your own inputs.
steps: Enter the loan amount and annual nominal rate.
Enter a whole number of repayment months and select a display currency.
Review the monthly payment, total repayment and interest.
tools.help: The monthly rate is the annual rate divided by twelve. Payments follow the standard equal-payment amortization formula; a zero-interest loan divides the principal evenly over the term. Terms from one to 1,200 months are accepted. This estimate assumes a fixed rate and monthly payments at the end of each period. Fees, insurance, taxes, early repayments and lender-specific rounding are excluded. Currency selection changes the display, not an exchange rate.

faq.question: Can I calculate an interest-free loan?
faq.answer: Yes. Set the annual rate to zero and the amount is divided across the chosen months.

faq.question: Does it include lender fees?
faq.answer: No. Entered principal and interest are used; fees and other charges must be assessed separately.

seo.title: Loan / EMI Calculator — Monthly Payment Estimate
seo.description: Estimate fixed monthly loan payments, total repayment and interest from your amount, annual rate and term. Fees, insurance and taxes are excluded.

tools.name: Savings Calculator
tools.description: Project your savings over time.
tools.intro: Project savings with an initial balance, monthly contributions and a constant annual return. Compare your contributions with the projected growth.
steps: Enter the starting balance and monthly contribution.
Choose a nominal annual return and a whole number of years.
Review the projected balance, deposits and growth.
tools.help: Returns compound monthly at the annual nominal rate divided by twelve. Monthly contributions are added at the end of each month. A zero return simply adds all contributions to the initial balance. The projection accepts one to 100 years and rejects totals beyond safe numerical limits. Constant returns are an assumption, not a forecast; market variation, fees, taxes and inflation are excluded.

faq.question: When are monthly contributions added?
faq.answer: At the end of each month, after that month’s growth.

faq.question: Is the projection a promised return?
faq.answer: No. It is a mathematical estimate using a constant rate supplied by you.

tools.name: Profit Calculator

tools.intro: Calculate profit or loss from revenue and total cost. Compare profit margin on revenue with markup on cost.
steps: Enter revenue and total cost in the same currency.
Choose a currency label if helpful.
Read the profit or loss, margin and markup.
tools.help: Profit is revenue minus cost. Margin divides profit by revenue; markup divides it by cost. A zero denominator is shown as not defined instead of an infinite percentage. Losses are supported. Include all relevant costs in your input; the tool does not infer expenses, taxes or accounting rules. Results display two decimal places and are numerical aids.

faq.question: Are margin and markup the same?
faq.answer: No. Margin is measured against revenue, while markup is measured against cost.

faq.question: Can I calculate a loss?
faq.answer: Yes. Revenue below cost produces a negative profit and negative percentages when defined.

seo.title: Profit Calculator — Margin, Markup and Loss

Enter a discount from 0 to 100 percent.
Read the amount saved and the final price.
tools.help: Savings equal original price × discount ÷ 100. Final price equals original price minus savings. All values use the same units or currency you entered; no exchange conversion is performed. Display rounds to two decimal places. Taxes, fees, delivery costs and sequential discounts are not included.

faq.question: Can I enter a decimal discount?

faq.question: Does this include sales tax?

faq.question: Can I account for unpaid weeks?

faq.question: Is Base64 encryption?

faq.question: Should I paste a whole URL?

faq.question: Why does a plus sign stay unchanged when decoding?

seo.title: URL Encoder & Decoder — Escape URL Components

tools.name: UUID Generator

faq.question: Which UUID version is generated?
faq.answer: Version 4, with the standard random UUID format and variant bits.

faq.question: Are UUIDs guaranteed to be unique?
faq.answer: No random identifier guarantees uniqueness. UUID v4 has an extremely large random space; applications should still enforce their own uniqueness rules.

faq.question: Are generated UUIDs stored?

seo.title: UUID Generator — Random Version 4 Identifiers

faq.question: Can I use a named CSS color or variable?

seo.title: Color Converter — HEX, RGB, HSL and Alpha

faq.question: Can I change the destination after printing?

faq.question: Does Tool Fera track scans?

tools.name: Password Generator

Select Generate password.
Copy the password and store it securely.
tools.help: Each password includes uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers and symbols. Characters are selected with rejection sampling to avoid modulo bias. Passwords are not saved to localStorage or sent to a server. Use a unique password for every account.

faq.question: Are the passwords generated randomly?
faq.answer: Yes. The tool uses crypto.getRandomValues and rejection sampling rather than Math.random.

faq.question: Does Tool Fera remember my passwords?
faq.answer: No. Passwords stay in page memory. Save a password in your own password manager before leaving.

seo.title: Password Generator — Cryptographic Browser Randomness
seo.description: Generate a random password from 12 to 64 characters, then copy it to your password manager. Generated passwords are not uploaded or saved in history.

tools.name: Random Number Generator
tools.description: Pick a number within your chosen range.
tools.intro: Generate integers within an inclusive range using your browser’s cryptographic random API. Allow repeats or request a batch of unique numbers.
steps: Enter the inclusive minimum and maximum.
Choose a count from one to 1,000 and optionally prevent repeats.
Generate, then copy or download one number per line.
tools.help: Bounds can range from minus one billion to one billion. Rejection sampling avoids modulo bias. Unique batches use bounded sampling without replacement followed by a random shuffle; they cannot request more values than the range contains. Values stay in page memory and are not logged or stored. A random output is not an official draw record or a replacement for independently audited selection procedures.

faq.question: Can the minimum or maximum appear?
faq.answer: Yes. Both bounds are included.

faq.question: Can a batch contain repeats?
faq.answer: Yes by default. Enable Unique numbers to prevent repeats within that batch.

seo.title: Random Number Generator — Choose Range and Count
seo.description: Generate random whole numbers within your chosen range using browser cryptographic randomness. Set the count and choose whether repeated values are allowed.

tools.name: Invoice Generator
tools.description: Create a clear invoice for your work.
tools.intro: Create a simple downloadable PDF invoice with your details, line items, discount, tax and payment notes. Everything is prepared on your device.
steps: Enter sender, recipient, invoice number and date.
Add descriptions, quantities and prices; set a currency, discount and your own tax rate.
Check totals, create the PDF, review it and download.
tools.help: Up to 30 line items are supported. Each quantity times unit price rounds to two decimal places, then line totals are summed. The discount is subtracted before the supplied tax percentage is applied and rounded. The PDF uses the existing local document engine with selectable text and tables. Font substitutions can affect uncommon scripts; review any warning and the downloaded file. You supply legally appropriate invoice details and rates. No payment collection, invoice database, automatic tax calculation or currency conversion is provided.

faq.question: Is tax calculated automatically for my country?
faq.answer: No. You enter the percentage. The generator does not select official tax rules or determine invoice compliance.

faq.question: Are invoices saved or sent to the recipient?
faq.answer: No. They remain in this page until you download them. Tool Fera does not email invoices or store them.

faq.question: When is the discount applied?
faq.answer: The discount reduces the subtotal before tax is applied.

seo.title: Invoice Generator — Download a Simple PDF Invoice
seo.description: Create a PDF invoice from your business details and line items. Review totals and download locally; Tool Fera does not store invoice records.

categories.name: PDF Tools
categories.description: Merge, split, rotate, delete or reorder PDF pages locally. Optimize a PDF, export PNG/JPG page images, combine PNG/JPG files or convert native PDF text into editable Word without a processing server.
categories.guide: Merging combines documents in your chosen order. Splitting extracts a selection into a new PDF; enter pages and ranges in the order you want them to appear. Rotate changes selected page orientations; Delete keeps the remaining pages; Reorder requires every page exactly once. Recommended, Strong compression and Best quality are the simple PDF compression levels. The tool first tries structural optimization, then a page-image copy when needed. Page-image results remove selectable text, links and forms; compare the actual savings and review the document. A larger or effectively unchanged output is not offered as a compressed success. PDF to PNG/JPG exports rendered page images; PNG/JPG to PDF embeds your images. PDF to Word preserves page boundaries using editable text containers and recoverable Word tables, with localized images for complex vector diagrams and charts. Font substitutions and unusual layouts may differ. Scanned PDFs use the separate PDF OCR workflow with mobile limits. Native PDF to Word and Word to PDF never invoke OCR. DOCX conversion preserves explicit and saved page breaks, section geometry and intentional spacing. Review complex layouts and recognition errors. PDF-to-image rendering and Word analysis run locally with PDF.js. Editing and page copying use open-source processing in a background worker. They copy page content, but interactive forms, bookmarks and digital signatures may not carry over. Password-protected files are unsupported. Review the downloaded document before sharing it.

faq.question: Do PDF files leave my device?
faq.answer: PDF editing uses pdf-lib in a browser worker; image rendering uses PDF.js locally. Your documents are not uploaded to Tool Fera or a third-party PDF API.

faq.question: Can I compress or convert a PDF to Word here?
faq.answer: Compression offers Recommended, Strong compression and Best quality. It first attempts structural optimization and can use a page-image copy when needed. Image-based compression removes selectable text, links and forms. PDF to Word reconstructs editable text, images and simple tables; scanned pages use the separate PDF OCR tool. Word to PDF accepts DOCX. Both work locally, and complex layouts may differ.

faq.question: Can I process a password-protected PDF?
faq.answer: No. Use an unencrypted copy you are authorized to process. This version does not remove passwords or preserve digital signatures.

seo.title: PDF Tools — Compress, Merge, Convert & OCR
seo.description: Edit PDF pages, reduce file size, convert PDF and DOCX, or recognize scanned text. Explore local browser tools with clear format and layout limitations.

categories.name: Image Tools
categories.description: Resize, crop, compress or convert images on your device, or extract English text with local OCR. Set exact dimensions, preserve proportions or crop to fit, choose an output format, and compare actual file sizes before downloading.
categories.guide: Use Fit to preserve proportions, Fill to crop the center, or Stretch for exact dimensions with possible distortion. JPEG is useful for photographs and fills transparency with white. PNG keeps transparency; WebP supports transparency and adjustable quality. AVIF export is offered only when your browser can encode it. BMP export is uncompressed and can be large. Image work runs in a background worker, with a smaller compatibility fallback for older browsers. Metadata and animation are not preserved.

faq.question: Which image formats can I open?
faq.answer: JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, BMP and GIF, subject to the browser’s decoder. GIF uses its first frame. HEIC and TIFF are not supported in this version.

faq.question: Which formats can I download?
faq.answer: JPEG, PNG, WebP and BMP. AVIF is available only if the browser passes an actual encoding check. Unsupported output types are not offered.

faq.question: Are images uploaded or stored?
faq.answer: No. Processing and temporary previews stay on your device. Reset or leave the page to release them. Only tool identifiers are saved in favorites and history.

seo.title: Image Tools — Compress, Resize, Crop & Convert
seo.description: Prepare images with local compression, resizing, cropping and format conversion. Extract English text with OCR and review previews before downloading.

categories.name: Student Tools
categories.description: Calculate GPA and CGPA, check marks and attendance, or build a custom admission aggregate. Use your own institution’s grade points and credit rules.
categories.guide: A course with more credits contributes more to your GPA. For a cumulative result, weight each semester GPA by its credits instead of taking a simple average. These calculators accept scales up to 10; use the grade points from your institution and check its repeat-course and rounding policies.

faq.question: Does the GPA calculator support different grading scales?
faq.answer: Yes. Enter your actual grade points on a scale up to 10, including the common 4.0 scale.

faq.question: Is a simple average the same as CGPA?
faq.answer: Only when every semester has the same number of credits. The CGPA calculator uses each semester’s credit total.

seo.title: Student Calculators — GPA, CGPA, Marks & Attendance
seo.description: Calculate weighted GPA, cumulative grades, marks, attendance and admission aggregates. Use your institution’s own credit, grade-point and weighting rules.

categories.name: Calculators

categories.description: Calculate percentages and estimate journey fuel costs with your own prices and units. Estimate loan payments, savings, profit, discounts and gross salary equivalents.
categories.guide: Start with the amount, unit and rate you intend to use. Our fuel calculator supports kilometres or miles, km/L, L/100 km, and US or Imperial MPG. Choose a country for sensible unit and currency defaults, or override the currency yourself. Enter your own fuel price; no live market rate is assumed. Results are estimates based on your inputs.

faq.question: Can I choose different fuel units?
faq.answer: Yes. Choose kilometres or miles for distance and km/L, L/100 km, US MPG or Imperial MPG for efficiency. Prices can be per litre, US gallon or Imperial gallon. Set the currency and enter your own price.

faq.question: Are financial results official quotes?
faq.answer: No. Calculators provide numerical estimates. Fees, taxes, actual vehicle consumption and other conditions can affect real costs.

seo.title: Free Calculators — Money, Fuel, Percentages & Age

categories.name: Text Tools
categories.description: Count words and Unicode characters, convert case, remove duplicate lines or clean whitespace. Check reading time and character limits without uploading or saving your text.
categories.guide: Words are counted as whitespace-separated tokens. Characters are counted by Unicode code point, with a separate total excluding whitespace. Some emoji contain multiple code points, and other applications may treat hyphenation differently. Use the rule required by your assignment or platform. Case conversion follows mechanical Unicode casing rules; review acronyms and names after converting.

faq.question: Is pasted text stored?
faq.answer: No. The available counters process text in the current page’s memory. Text is not uploaded or stored in your history.

faq.question: Why might counts differ from another editor?
faq.answer: Editors use different rules for punctuation, word boundaries and emoji. This tool states its counting rules so you can compare them.

seo.title: Text Tools — Count, Convert Case & Clean Lines
seo.description: Count words and Unicode characters, convert text case, remove duplicate lines and clean whitespace. Your writing stays in the browser.

categories.name: Developer Tools
categories.description: Generate random UUIDs, convert HEX/RGB/HSL colors, format JSON, encode and decode Base64 text, or escape URL components locally. See clear syntax errors and copy the result without sending your data to an external formatting service.
categories.guide: JSON requires double-quoted keys and strings and does not allow comments or trailing commas. Formatting changes presentation, while parsing follows JavaScript semantics. Very large integers can lose precision; keep precision-sensitive identifiers as strings or use a specialized parser. Base64 is reversible UTF-8 text encoding, not encryption. URL encoding escapes a single component; it should not be applied to an entire URL.

faq.question: Does the formatter validate JSON?
faq.answer: Yes. Invalid input produces a visible error. Valid input can be formatted or minified.

faq.question: Is my JSON sent to a server?
faq.answer: No. Parsing and formatting happen locally in your browser.

seo.title: Developer Tools — JSON, Base64, URLs, UUIDs & Colors
seo.description: Format JSON, encode UTF-8 and URL components, generate UUIDs and convert color formats locally. Check errors and copy usable results.
